newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU might not take part in Bosnia aid conference.
newsitem.headline: EU might not take part in Bosnia aid conference.

text.p: The European Union said on Wednesday it might not participate in a planned donor conference for Bosnia-Herzegovina, unless an International Monetary Fund agreement was struck first.

"We need to be confident that the right framework for assistance is in place," the EU's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said in a statement. "Therefore there can only be a new donor conference if there is a quick agreement with the International Monetary Fund."
"The quick start package of laws adopted on June 22 is a step in the right direction," he added.
The EU executive said in the statement that its reservations were due to concerns that the reconstruction effort in Bosnia-Herzegovina was being hampered by political divisions in the country.

The 15-nation bloc, the world's largest single donor to the former Yugoslav state, in 1996 allocated 310 million ecus in grant aid aiming at facilitating the return of refugees, reviving the economy, support the building of new institutions and humanitarian aid.
The Commission said one of the most urgent problems to tackle was the organisation of the return of 600,000 war refugees currently living in the EU member states.
